name: Tuairisgeal

attributes.attribute: a Scottish figure who lured the king of Ireland into gambling

sources: McKay, John G. More West Highland Tales. Vol. 2. Scottish Anthropological and Folklore Society. Edinburgh: Oliver and Boyd, 1969, 3.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The king of Ireland met Tuairisgeal while riding in Scotland. The strange man lured him into gambling. Tuairisgeal seemed an easy mark, for he lost his wife first, then his horse. On the third wager Tuairisgeal won and could make any request of the king. He wanted a single answer, the truth of how his own father had died. The king learned that the father was a monster who had turned children into wolves. When the monster seized his daughter, angry wolves who were her transformed brothers and sisters came to her aid.

okr.objective: Record the Scottish folkloric figure Tuairisgeal.
